Assessment:
- Clinical impression: Probable uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis).
  - Justification: Several days of dysuria and lower abdominal crampy pain, small amount of hematuria, absence of fever or flank/back pain.
- Conflict noted:
  - Brief unclear exchange about fever ("think so" then clarified as "no fever") — conflict noted.

Plan:
- Immediate actions advised/taken:
  - Plan to prescribe a short course of antibiotics; options discussed: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim. Provider stated regimen: one tablet twice daily for three days (specific antibiotic choice not documented).
  - Advice to drink plenty of fluids.
  - Suggestion that cranberry juice can sometimes help symptoms.
- Specific instructions to patient:
  - Avoid sexual intercourse while symptoms are resolving if possible; continue using barrier contraception (condoms) if sexual activity occurs.
  - If symptoms have not improved by the end of the week, call or return for reassessment.
  - Call back if developing high temperature, back pain, or feeling generally more unwell (concern for possible upward spread to kidneys).
- Escalation criteria / red flags:
  - High temperature/fever.
  - New or worsening back/flank pain.
  - Increasing systemic unwellness.
  - Failure to improve by end of week.
- Follow-up:
  - Return visit or phone call if no improvement or if red-flag symptoms develop.
  - No ENT/allergy referral, auto-injector discussion, or urine testing (dipstick/urine culture) documented in the transcript.
- Emergency contact instruction (exact phrasing from transcript):
  - "I want you to give me a call or come back and see me."
  - "Do give me a call if you're having any concerns, OK."
